themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge in East Harlem
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked 700% this week (16 complaints vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), signaling a rapid deterioration in street conditions and possible homelessness crisis affecting public spaces across CD111.
evidence: 16 encampment complaints filed last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 8.44, severity: high)
Represents 700% increase from baseline in a single week
No recent media coverage or community board discussion yet—emerging story
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: visit locations where encampments were reported to document conditions and interview unhoused residents about what triggered the influx
Policy angle: has the city reduced shelter capacity or transit services to East Harlem; coordinate with advocates and DHS for response timeline

themes_detail.label: Graffiti & Vandalism Wave
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped 1020% this week (7 complaints vs. 0.6 weekly average) and illegal tree damage spiked 700% three weeks ago (3 vs. 0.4 average), indicating coordinated or systemic property damage; community board has repeatedly requested graffiti removal funding.
evidence: Graffiti complaints: 7 this week vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 6.43)
Illegal tree damage: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.77)
Community board has filed recurring budget requests for 'Increase Graffiti Removal/Cleaning' (Agency: DSNY)—long-standing unmet need
reporting_angles: Investigate if graffiti spike is gang-related tagging, protest art, or opportunistic vandalism—interview NYPD and community activists
Accountability angle: DSNY response time to graffiti removal requests; check if budget constraints are delaying cleanup

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity & Street Safety
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints surged 300% this week (9 complaints vs. 2.2 weekly average), paired with a 700% spike in encampments, suggesting an emerging public health and safety nexus that requires rapid intervention.
evidence: Drug activity complaints: 9 this week vs. 2.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.56, severity: high)
Concurrent with encampment surge (16 complaints, up 700%), suggesting possible relationship
Community board budget requests include hiring additional traffic enforcement agents—signals historic underpolicing concerns
reporting_angles: Source interviews with NYPD Narcotics Unit and local precinct on whether this is new activity or reporting artifact
Community health angle: interview local clinics, harm reduction orgs, and residents on naloxone availability and overdose rates

themes_detail.label: Litter & Environmental Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests exploded 2300% this week (3 complaints vs. 0.1 weekly average) and dead animal complaints spiked 1100% (3 vs. 0.2 average), painting a picture of rapidly deteriorating sanitation conditions tied to possible budget or staffing failures.
evidence: Litter basket requests: 3 this week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69, severity: high, 2300% increase)
Dead animal complaints: 3 this week vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, severity: high, 1100% increase)
DSNY budget requests for 'Graffiti Removal/Cleaning' and DEP requests suggest chronic infrastructure underinvestment
reporting_angles: DSNY operations check: are sanitation routes being cut or delayed in CD111; interview union representatives and supervisors
Residents' quality-of-life angle: talk to block associations and merchants on street conditions and whether this is new or long-standing neglect

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise & Nuisance Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints jumped 167% this week (20 complaints vs. 7.5 weekly average), adding to existing chronic noise burden (2,115 residential noise complaints over 90 days), and community board has requested additional traffic enforcement agents—signaling coordination failure.
evidence: Vehicle noise complaints: 20 this week vs. 7.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.69, 167% spike)
Noise - Residential: 2,115 complaints over 90 days (2nd highest complaint type after heat/hot water)
Community board has filed recurring budget request to 'Hire additional traffic enforcement agents' (NYPD)—suggests known staffing gap
reporting_angles: Traffic enforcement audit: how many traffic agents are assigned to CD111 and are enforcement priorities aligned with 311 data
Resident impact: interview residents along high-traffic corridors (e.g., E. 125th St., Park Ave) on sleep disruption and quality of life
